name: Codex
description: Codex is a coding-agent surface of ChatGPT (not a standalone product), included with ChatGPT paid plans with no separate subscription. It is accessed at chatgpt.com/codex and through dedicated surfaces — the flagship desktop app (computer use, memory, 90+ plugins, in-app browser, Goal mode), plus CLI, IDE extension, and Chrome extension — performing multi-file code generation, editing, debugging, and agentic task execution using OpenAI frontier models.

writing-chat.summary: Codex accepts natural language prompts to generate, explain, and edit code. The CLI provides an interactive terminal chat experience while the cloud agent processes tasks asynchronously with full context.

subFeatures.name: Natural Language to Code
subFeatures.description: Describe what you want in plain English and Codex generates the corresponding code, including boilerplate, tests, and documentation

subFeatures.name: Interactive CLI Chat
subFeatures.description: Terminal-based conversational interface where you can iteratively refine code through multi-turn dialogue with the agent

subFeatures.name: Code Explanation
subFeatures.description: Ask Codex to explain existing code, trace logic, and document functions in natural language

limitations: CLI is terminal-only — no GUI or web chat interface
Cloud agent responses are asynchronous, not real-time streaming
Context limited to repository files and conversation history
No general-purpose writing — optimized specifically for code-related tasks

pricingTiers.details: Codex included for a limited time (promotional as of May 2026) with limited usage; CLI also usable with your own OpenAI API key (token billing)
Codex included; GPT-5.5 / GPT-5.4 / GPT-5.4-mini / GPT-5.3-Codex within ChatGPT subscription (no separate Codex subscription)
Included; 5x Plus usage at $100, 20x Plus usage at $200; GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark research preview
Included with larger VMs and admin controls; pay-as-you-go Codex-only seats (token billing) available

versionHistory.changes: GPT-5.5 added to the Codex model lineup as the default
Desktop Codex app released; GPT-5.3-Codex and GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark models launched
Cloud-based coding agent with sandbox execution, parallel task processing (Pro research preview 2025-05-16, Plus 2025-06-03)
Open-source CLI tool released on GitHub for terminal-based coding assistance

research.summary: Since the April 2026 'Codex for almost everything' update, Codex has a built-in in-app browser and is explicitly pitched for research workflows, in addition to navigating the local codebase. Research support is partial — it is centered on the desktop app's browsing rather than a dedicated Deep Research feature.

subFeatures.name: In-App Browser
subFeatures.description: Desktop Codex can browse the web with a built-in browser and users can annotate pages directly, enabling research workflows (added in the 2026-04-16 update)

subFeatures.name: Codebase Search
subFeatures.description: Codex can search and navigate the local repository to find relevant files, functions, and patterns

limitations: Browsing/research is centered on the desktop app, not all surfaces
No dedicated multi-source Deep Research report feature like ChatGPT's web app
Research is oriented toward coding and product workflows

pricingTiers.details: In-app browser and research workflows via the Codex desktop app, included with ChatGPT paid plans

versionHistory.changes: Added in-app browser and research workflows to the Codex desktop app

file-analysis.summary: Codex reads and analyzes files across the entire repository within its sandbox, understanding project structure, dependencies, and code relationships for informed code changes.

subFeatures.name: Repository-Wide File Reading
subFeatures.description: Reads any file in the cloned repository including source code, configuration, documentation, and data files

subFeatures.name: Dependency Analysis
subFeatures.description: Parses package manifests, import graphs, and build configurations to understand project dependencies

subFeatures.name: Multi-File Context
subFeatures.description: Analyzes relationships between files to make changes that are consistent across the entire codebase

limitations: Limited to files within the repository — cannot analyze external files or URLs
Binary file analysis limited to recognized formats
Large repositories may exceed context window limitations
No image or media file analysis

pricingTiers.details: Full local file access using your API key
Repository cloned into sandbox with full file access

versionHistory.changes: Sandboxed repository access with full file system navigation

document-creation.summary: Codex generates documentation, README files, code comments, and technical specifications as part of its coding workflow. It creates files directly in the repository.

subFeatures.name: README and Documentation Generation
subFeatures.description: Generates project documentation, README files, API docs, and inline code comments based on the codebase

subFeatures.name: Code Comment Generation
subFeatures.description: Adds JSDoc, docstrings, and inline comments explaining code logic and function signatures

limitations: Output limited to text-based files — no PDFs, presentations, or formatted documents
Documentation style follows model defaults unless explicitly instructed
Cannot generate diagrams or visual documentation

pricingTiers.details: Documentation generation as part of coding tasks
Documentation generation included in cloud agent tasks

versionHistory.changes: Documentation generation as part of multi-file coding tasks

image-generation.summary: Image generation was added to the Codex desktop app in the April 2026 'Codex for almost everything' update, using gpt-image-1.5 for product concept and mockup visuals. Support is partial — limited to the desktop app surface.

subFeatures.name: Mockup and Concept Image Generation
subFeatures.description: Desktop Codex uses gpt-image-1.5 to generate product concept and mockup visuals as part of coding and design workflows (added 2026-04-16)

limitations: Image generation is available only in the Codex desktop app, not the CLI, IDE extension, or web surface
Oriented toward product concepts and mockups rather than general-purpose art
Uses gpt-image-1.5 (not the ChatGPT web app's image stack)

pricingTiers.details: Image generation in the Codex desktop app, included with ChatGPT paid plans

versionHistory.changes: Added gpt-image-1.5 image generation to the Codex desktop app

prototyping.summary: Codex excels at code prototyping — generating full implementations from natural language descriptions, scaffolding new projects, creating proof-of-concept code, and iterating through multi-turn refinement.

subFeatures.name: Full Project Scaffolding
subFeatures.description: Generate entire project structures including source files, configuration, tests, and build scripts from a description

subFeatures.name: Multi-File Code Generation
subFeatures.description: Create coordinated changes across multiple files simultaneously, maintaining consistency across the codebase

subFeatures.name: Sandbox Code Execution
subFeatures.description: Cloud agent runs generated code in a sandboxed environment to verify it compiles and passes tests before presenting results

subFeatures.name: Test Generation
subFeatures.description: Automatically generate unit tests, integration tests, and test fixtures alongside implementation code

limitations: CLI version cannot execute code — only generates it
Cloud sandbox limited to standard development environments
Cannot start local servers or access network services during sandbox execution
Generated code quality depends on prompt specificity

pricingTiers.details: Code generation and scaffolding via API key
Code generation with sandbox execution and verification

versionHistory.changes: Sandboxed execution environment for verifying generated code

personalization.summary: Codex supports project configuration files and custom instructions plus, since the April 2026 desktop update, cross-session memory that remembers preferences, recurring workflows, and tech stacks.

subFeatures.name: Project Configuration
subFeatures.description: CODEX.md or similar configuration files in the repository root define project-specific instructions, coding conventions, and constraints

subFeatures.name: Model Selection
subFeatures.description: Choose between Codex models — GPT-5.5 (default), GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4-mini, and GPT-5.3-Codex (plus GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark on Pro) — based on task complexity and cost preferences

subFeatures.name: Memory
subFeatures.description: Desktop Codex remembers preferences, recurring workflows, and tech stacks across sessions (added 2026-04-16; personalization rolling out to Enterprise, Edu, and EU/UK users in May 2026)

limitations: Cross-session memory is centered on the desktop app
Configuration limited to project-level files
Personalization still rolling out to Enterprise, Edu, and EU/UK regions as of May 2026

pricingTiers.details: Project configuration, model selection, and cross-session memory included with ChatGPT paid plans

versionHistory.changes: Added cross-session memory (preferences, workflows, tech stacks) to the desktop app
Project configuration file support for customizing agent behavior

persistent-context.summary: Codex maintains context within a session through conversation history and repository-level configuration. The cloud agent persists task history and results within a workspace.

subFeatures.name: Session Conversation History
subFeatures.description: CLI maintains conversation context within a single terminal session for iterative refinement

subFeatures.name: Repository Context
subFeatures.description: Project configuration files and codebase serve as persistent context that informs every interaction

subFeatures.name: Cloud Task History
subFeatures.description: Codex Cloud maintains a history of completed tasks and their results within the workspace

limitations: CLI session context lost when terminal is closed
No cross-session memory in CLI mode
Cloud task history is per-workspace, not cross-project
No semantic memory or learned preferences

pricingTiers.details: Session-level context with repository configuration
Persistent task history within workspace

versionHistory.changes: Workspace-level task history and persistent context

agents.summary: Codex is fundamentally an agentic coding tool. Agents autonomously plan, write, test, and commit code changes in sandboxed environments and run multiple tasks in parallel. The April 2026 desktop app adds computer use (its own cursor across Mac apps) and Goal mode (work toward a defined outcome across turns).

subFeatures.name: Autonomous Code Agent
subFeatures.description: Agent independently reads the codebase, plans changes, writes code, runs tests, and presents verified results as a pull request or diff

subFeatures.name: Computer Use
subFeatures.description: Desktop Codex can see, click, and type with its own cursor across all Mac apps, with multiple agents running in parallel without interfering with the user's own work (added 2026-04-16)

subFeatures.name: Goal Mode
subFeatures.description: Define an outcome plus success criteria and Codex works toward it across turns; available in the desktop app, IDE extension, and CLI (GA 2026-04-16)

subFeatures.name: Parallel Task Processing
subFeatures.description: Run multiple coding tasks simultaneously, each in an isolated sandbox environment

subFeatures.name: Agentic Tool Use
subFeatures.description: Agent uses shell commands, file operations, test runners, linters, and 90+ plugins (Skills, app integrations, MCP servers) autonomously to complete tasks

limitations: Cloud sandbox has limited internet access — cannot install packages not already in the repo
Computer use is limited to the desktop app (Mac apps)
Task scope generally limited to single-repository changes
Human review required before merging agent-generated changes

pricingTiers.details: Limited agentic coding included for a limited time (promotional); CLI also via API key
Agentic coding included with ChatGPT subscription; parallel agents and sandbox execution
5x Plus usage at $100, 20x at $200; GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark research preview
Larger VMs and admin controls; pay-as-you-go Codex-only seats available

versionHistory.changes: Desktop app adds computer use, Goal mode GA, 90+ plugins (Skills, app integrations, MCP servers)
Cloud-based autonomous coding agent with parallel task execution
Terminal-based agentic coding with tool use

connectors.summary: Codex integrates with GitHub for repository access and pull requests, runs as an IDE extension and Chrome extension, and (since the April 2026 desktop update) supports 90+ plugins including Atlassian Rovo, CircleCI, CodeRabbit, GitLab Issues, Microsoft Suite, Neon by Databricks, Remotion, and Render via Skills, app integrations, and MCP servers.

subFeatures.name: GitHub Integration
subFeatures.description: Agent clones repositories from GitHub, creates branches, and opens pull requests with completed changes

subFeatures.name: 90+ Plugins (Skills, App Integrations, MCP)
subFeatures.description: Desktop Codex connects to 90+ plugins including Atlassian Rovo, CircleCI, CodeRabbit, GitLab Issues, Microsoft Suite, Neon by Databricks, Remotion, and Render (added 2026-04-16)

subFeatures.name: ChatGPT and Multi-Surface Access
subFeatures.description: Codex tasks can be initiated from chatgpt.com/codex and across the desktop app, IDE extension, and Chrome extension, all gated by a ChatGPT plan

limitations: Full 90+ plugin catalog is centered on the desktop app
GitHub is the primary version-control integration
CLI operates on the local filesystem
All surfaces require ChatGPT plan credentials

pricingTiers.details: GitHub integration, IDE/Chrome extensions, and 90+ plugins included with ChatGPT paid plans

versionHistory.changes: Added 90+ plugins (Skills, app integrations, MCP servers) and in-app browser to the desktop app
GitHub repository integration with PR workflow

dictation.summary: Codex is a text-based coding tool with no voice input or dictation capabilities.

subFeatures.name: Not Available
subFeatures.description: Codex operates entirely through text-based CLI or web interface — no voice input support

limitations: No voice input or speech-to-text integration
No audio processing capabilities
Terminal-based interface is text-only

pricingTiers.details: Not available
